reason: Bun reports transitive Picomatch versions from frontend tooling. pnpm holds both affected majors on patched releases through the ranged pnpm.overrides entries, but Bun ignores ranged resolution keys such as 'picomatch@<2.3.2', so bun.lock keeps 2.3.1 and 4.0.3. Re-verified against Bun 1.3.11 on 2026-09-14: the ranged key still leaves anymatch, micromatch and readdirp on 2.3.1, and the only key Bun does honour, a bare 'picomatch', collapses the tree onto 4.0.7 and breaks those three consumers, which each declare ^2.x. Tracked in https://github.com/leynos/wildside/issues/492; revisit when Bun supports ranged resolutions or the tooling drops Picomatch 2.

Both pnpm and Bun report this, so the entry is scoped to the frontend-pwa workspace ledger. extract-zip has no patched release; 2.0.1 is the latest published version and the advisory covers everything up to it. It reaches the tree only through puppeteer 23 via @puppeteer/browsers 2.x, which is used at build time to download a Mermaid rendering browser from Google's own endpoints, so no untrusted archive is extracted. The fix is @puppeteer/browsers 3.x, which replaced extract-zip with modern-tar and first ships in puppeteer 25.7; that is a two-major bump and scripts/install-mermaid-browser.mjs deep-imports puppeteer internals, so it needs its own change and verification. Tracked in https://github.com/leynos/wildside/issues/491.

A second, independent advisory against the same unpatchable extract-zip 2.0.1 that EXTRACT_ZIP_SYMLINK_TRAVERSAL_2026_08 covers, reported by both pnpm and Bun. The symlink entries it describes are written only while @puppeteer/browsers 2.x unpacks a Chrome archive that puppeteer itself fetched from Google's endpoints at build time, so no attacker-supplied archive reaches it. It resolves with the same puppeteer 25.7 upgrade and must not outlive it. Tracked in https://github.com/leynos/wildside/issues/491.

Development-time tooling only. braces reaches the tree through chokidar@3.6.0 and micromatch@4.0.8, which both pin braces@3.0.3 in pnpm-lock.yaml. The brace patterns come from repository-controlled configuration, not runtime user input, but pull requests can change that configuration and cause their own CI build to fail. The advisory (published 2026-09-18, stack exhaustion on deeply nested patterns) covers every release up to 3.0.3, which is the latest published, so there is no patched release to move to. Tracked in https://github.com/leynos/wildside/issues/527; remove this entry once a patched braces exists or chokidar and micromatch drop braces 3.

Build-time design-token generation only, reported by both pnpm and Bun, so the entry is scoped to the frontend-pwa workspace ledger. deepmerge reaches the tree only through style-dictionary@5.6.0 via @bundled-es-modules/deepmerge@4.3.2, which packages/tokens runs from its postinstall and build scripts to emit tokens. The advisory (prototype poisoning of the returned object, low severity, published 2026-09-18) covers every release from 4.2.0 to 4.3.1, and 4.3.1 is the latest published, so no patched release exists to move to. Every style-dictionary release through 5.7.1 still declares @bundled-es-modules/deepmerge ^4.3.2, so bumping it does not help. The merged objects are repository-controlled token definitions rather than runtime user input, and nothing from this path is served to a browser tab. Tracked in https://github.com/leynos/wildside/issues/570; remove this entry once deepmerge publishes a patch and style-dictionary adopts it, or once tokens stop depending on style-dictionary.

zod is patched only in 4.6.6 and above, and the workspace is on zod 3.25.76 (`^3` in frontend-pwa and packages/types), so the fix is a major-version migration that needs its own change and verification rather than a pin bump. The advisory is memory exhaustion while validating a very large array against an array schema with no length constraint. The only array schema is UsersSchema in packages/types/src/user.ts, applied by customFetchParsed in frontend-pwa/src/api/fetcher.ts to responses from the project's own backend and running in the user's browser tab, so an attacker would need to control the backend response, and the impact is a client-side memory exhaustion of one tab, not a server compromise. The other path, puppeteer > chromium-bidi > zod, is build-time Mermaid rendering tooling that never parses untrusted input. The entry expires after 14 days. Tracked in https://github.com/leynos/wildside/issues/561.

Development-time tooling only, reported by both pnpm and Bun, so the entry is scoped to the frontend-pwa workspace ledger. The advisory (denial of service through globparts amplification) is patched only in minimatch 11.0.1, and glob 14 already takes the patched copy. The two other consumers declare the 10.x line: typedoc 0.28.20 (`^10.2.5`, the latest release) and markdownlint-cli 0.48.0 (`~10.2.6`, the latest release). Forcing typedoc onto 11 fails its documentation gate (`mini.matchOne is not a function`), so a pin bump is not available. Both match glob patterns taken from repository-controlled configuration (typedoc entry points, markdownlint file selections), not runtime user input, and nothing from either path is served to a browser tab or runs in production. Tracked in https://github.com/leynos/wildside/issues/575; remove this entry once typedoc and markdownlint-cli accept minimatch 11 or drop it.
